Voice Coach — Implementation Design — Vi.sectionTitle: The stochastic engine — why gaps vary but never runs dry
Voice Coach — Implementation Design — Vi.quote:
💡 FROM YOUR NOTE — SHOULD A CLEANER REP EARN MORE?

Right now "clean" is binary, so every clean rep has the same praise odds: unpredictable, but flat. Your instinct — a super-clean rep should earn more — is a good one and cheap to add. Feed the rep's 0–1 form score into the praise chance (better rep → higher odds) and bias the line pool toward the bigger praise ("Tốt lắm!") on standout reps, the smaller ones ("Tốt") on ordinary ones. It stays variable-ratio — quality tilts the dice, it doesn't make praise predictable. And it answers your other question directly: yes, it's genuinely unpredictable (a fresh random draw every rep), but with this change a flawless rep would be more likely to get noticed, which is exactly what a real trainer does. Tracked as D8.

Hustle — hesitation-armed, commit-fired.quote:
Q1 · THE "CHÍN — CỐ LÊN!" PAIRING CHANGES SHAPE

Commit-firing means the count and the push no longer land together
In the old post-rep model, count + hustle fired at the same instant ("Chín — cố lên!"). In the commit-fired model, the count for rep 9 fires when rep 9 lands at the bottom, and the push fires when rep 10 starts at the raise — on either side of the hesitation. So they're sequential now: "Chín… [rest]… Một cái nữa thôi!". The co-occurrence machinery is preserved (count is not an outcome cue, so it never blocks or is blocked by hustle) — but in glute's timing they simply happen at different moments.

A
Sequential is correct and better — it mirrors a real coach: count the rep, watch the hesitation, then push into the commit. (My read.)
B
You actually want them simultaneous — then hustle would need a different moment, which reopens the commit-fired decision. Flag it.

Q2 · THE INFLATED-BASELINE FAILURE MODE

Accept it for v1, or clamp the baseline now?
A set that's hard from the first rep inflates its own baseline, so the grind never reads as stretched and hustle stays silent on exactly the set it's for (§04).

A
Accept for v1, instrument, revisit with Stage-B data — we never false-fire, and the calibration run will show whether it's real before we add a knob.
B
Clamp the baseline to a ceiling now — costs one more uncalibrated number up front.
Strict drop — a late "one more!" is worse than none; the armed gap is long so this rarely binds anyway.

Q4 · RISE-PHASE IDENTITY ON VOICESCRIPT

Setup / tracking-safety voice · design f.quote:
tate per class C:  CLEAR | LATCHED | LATCHED_RECUED
timers per class C: conditionTrueSince, conditionClearSince

each frame, given C's condition = present/absent this frame:

  CLEAR:
    if present for ≥ ENTER_DEBOUNCE_MS (~1s continuous):   // flicker guard
        request(C)              // enqueue into the single slot, latest-wins
        state = LATCHED; latchedSince = now
    // brief flicker to present-then-absent never crosses the debounce -> no fire

  LATCHED:
    if absent for ≥ EXIT_DEBOUNCE_MS (~1s continuous):
        state = CLEAR           // re-armed; a genuine RE-ENTRY will fire again
    else if still present for ≥ RE_CUE_MS (~10s since latchedSince):
        request(C, fuller=true) // ONE fuller re-cue, then quiet for real
        state = LATCHED_RECUED

  LATCHED_RECUED:
    if absent for ≥ EXIT_DEBOUNCE_MS: state = CLEAR   // only exit is clearing
    // never fires again while continuously latched
